710612.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ptólis, from Proto-Indo-European *tpólHis, from *tpelH- (“fortification; city”). The early form πτόλις (ptólis) shows metathesis tp > pt because Ancient Greek stop clusters always end in a coronal.

710672.t: From πορνεύω (porneúō, “to prostitute, to whore”) + -ία (-íā, “-ia: forming abstract nouns”), from πόρνη (pórnē, “prostitute, whore”) + -εύω (-eúō, forming verbs), from the Proto-Indo-European root *perh₂- (“to sell, to provide for a fee”).

710646.t: From Proto-Indo-European *polh₁ús (“much, many”), o-grade derivative of the root *pleh₁- (“to fill”).

710693.t: Uncertain, though most theories imply a derivation from Proto-Indo-European *peth₂- (“to spread out; to fly”) by relating the term to reflexes as such: * πίπτω (pī́ptō, “to fall”), thus a "waterfall" > "river that sweeps things away", * πετάννυμι…

710616.t: From πόλις (pólis, “city”) + -της (-tēs). The ι from the stem of πόλις led to the backformation -ίτης (-ī́tēs), whence the reanalysis πολ-ίτης (pol-ī́tēs).

710605.t: According to Beekes, of Pre-Greek origin, as suggested by πτ ~ π (pt ~ p) variation in its variants.

710661.t: According to Beekes, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)penh₁- (“to weave, to twist”), with semantic shift "weaving, stretching" > "tensing, strain" > "exertion, toil".

710691.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pótis, from Proto-Indo-European *pótis. Cognates include Albanian pata, Latin potis and Sanskrit पति॑ (páti).

710664.t: From Proto-Hellenic *póntos, from Proto-Indo-European *pónteh₁s (“path, road”). Cognates include Sanskrit पन्था (pánthā-, “way”), Old Armenian հուն (hun, “riverbed”), Latin pōns (“bridge”), and Old English findan (English find).

710696.t: Proto-Hellenic *kʷókʷe, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷókʷe, from *kʷos + *-kʷe, equivalent to πο- (po-) + τε (te). See its indefinite form ποτέ (poté).

710697.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʷóteros, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷóteros, from *kʷos (“which”) + *-teros (contrastive suffix).

710675.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pórnē, from the Proto-Indo-European root *perh₂- (“to sell”), which also gave the verb πέρνημι (pérnēmĭ, “to sell”).

710692.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʷotsos, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷóti, adverb from *kʷos (“what”). Compare the indefinite form ποσός (posós).

710682.t: Traditionally derived from πορφύρω (porphúrō, “(of waves) to heave, boil, surge up”), itself related to φύρω (phúrō, “to mix”), Hittite 𒁍𒊒𒌓 (purut, “mud, soil”) and Sanskrit भुरति (bhuráti, “have convulsions, sprawl”).

710611.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pol͏̌l͏̌ós, from Proto-Indo-European *pol-yós, from the root *pelH- (“pale, gray”).

710600.t: From πέκω (pékō, “to comb, to card; to shear”) + -ος (-os).

710683.t: From πορφύρα (porphúrā) + -εος (-eos), of unknown, perhaps Semitic, origin. The association with πορφύρω (porphúrō, “to surge up (of waves)”), through an association with the “wine-dark sea”, is a folk etymology.

710679.t: Neither a reduplicated form from πείρω (peírō, “to pierce”), nor a creation from πόρκης (pórkēs, “ring around the shaft of a spear”) makes sense.

710681.t: From πόρρω (pórrhō), Attic form of πρόσω (prósō) + -θεν (-then, “from”).

710669.t: From the o-grade of πέρθω (pérthō) + -έω (-éō, frequentative suffix).
